title: Ordering Numbers to 10,000
introduction: Develop Primary 3 skills in ordering numbers to 10,000.
definition: Compare digits starting from the highest place value. At the first different digit, the larger digit identifies the larger number. Ascending means smallest to largest; descending means largest to smallest.

exercises.question: Larger: 7,308 or 7,380?
exercises.solution: Both have 7 thousands and 3 hundreds; 8 tens > 0 tens, so 7,380 > 7,308.

exercises.question: Smaller: 5,099 or 5,900?
exercises.solution: Both have 5 thousands; 0 hundreds < 9 hundreds, so 5,099 < 5,900.

exercises.question: Largest of 3,810, 3,801, 3,180?
exercises.solution: 3,810 and 3,801 have 8 hundreds; 3,810 has more tens. 3,810 > 3,801 > 3,180.

exercises.question: Smallest of 7,502, 7,205, 7,520?
exercises.solution: All have 7 thousands; 7,205 has only 2 hundreds while the others have 5. 7,205 < 7,502 < 7,520.

summary: Compare digits starting from the highest place value. At the first different digit, the larger digit identifies the larger number. Ascending means smallest to largest; descending means largest to smallest.
